story_name: Horus's Rightful Throne: Justice and Reclamation
character_description: Horus, falcon-headed god with piercing amber eyes that see all truths, bronze skin glowing with warrior's intensity, bearing scars from battles fought for his birthright. His form embodies both fierce warrior and rightful heir—power earned through struggle rather than inherited.
setting: Egyptian kingdoms fighting for justice and rightful authority
theme: Reclaiming what was stolen through courage, persistence, and refusal to accept injustice

video_prompts: Horus born in hiding—child of murdered father Osiris, raised in sanctuary to reclaim stolen throne.
first_frame_prompt: Horus manifests as warrior-child in sanctuary, amber eyes already fierce with awareness of theft done to his father. Falcon-headed form represents connection to sky, to vision, to rising above. Bronze skin bears marks of training for battles ahead. His mother Isis has taught him that his birthright was stolen and his role is reclamation, not acceptance of theft.
speech: My father was murdered. My throne was stolen. I will reclaim what belongs to me.

video_prompts: Horus loses eye in battle—sacrifice that strengthens his resolve rather than defeating it.
first_frame_prompt: Horus in greatest battle loses one eye to Set. The loss is devastation—yet becomes transformation. Amber eye remaining burns brighter with clarity. Falcon-headed form seems to pierce through all illusion. His missing eye represents cost of justice—and his refusal to let cost defeat him. He loses sight of flesh while gaining sight of truth.
speech: You took my eye. But you cannot take my vision.
